title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
theoryHTML:
1. Present Simple (Routines & Facts)

We use the Present Simple to talk about things we do every day, habits, routines, or things that are always true.

  • Keywords: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays.
I play Minecraft every evening.
She never eats vegetables.
Water boils at 100 degrees.

2. Present Continuous (Happening NOW)

We use the Present Continuous (verb to be + verb-ing) to talk about actions that are happening right at this exact moment.

  • Keywords: now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen!
Look! The dog is sleeping on the sofa.
I am doing my homework right now.

3. Present Continuous (Future Plans)

We ALSO use the Present Continuous to talk about future plans that are already organized or fixed.

  • Keywords: tonight, tomorrow, this afternoon, next weekend.
I am playing football with my friends this afternoon. (It is a plan!)
We are traveling to London tomorrow.

questions.text: I usually ___ cereal for breakfast, but today I am eating toast.
questions.explanation: 'Usually' indicates a routine or habit, so we use the Present Simple ('eat').

questions.text: Shh! The baby ___ in the bedroom.
questions.explanation: 'Shh!' means the action is happening right now, so we use Present Continuous ('is sleeping').

questions.text: We ___ a movie at the cinema this evening. I have the tickets!
questions.explanation: 'This evening' and having the tickets means it's a fixed future plan. We use Present Continuous ('are watching').

questions.text: My dad ___ to work by car every morning.
questions.explanation: 'Every morning' is a routine. For 'He/She/It' in Present Simple, we add -s or -es ('goes').

questions.text: Look! The boys ___ football in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' tells us the action is happening right now. We use Present Continuous ('are playing').

questions.text: I ___ to the dentist tomorrow at 5:00 PM.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow at 5:00 PM' is a fixed future arrangement, so we use Present Continuous ('am going').

questions.text: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: This is a scientific fact that is always true. We use Present Simple ('boils').

questions.text: What ___ right now?
questions.explanation: 'Right now' indicates an action in progress. We use Present Continuous ('are you doing').

questions.text: They ___ basketball on Tuesdays.
questions.explanation: 'On Tuesdays' is a weekly routine. We use Present Simple ('play').

questions.text: I can't talk right now. I ___ my homework.
questions.explanation: 'I can't talk right now' means the action is happening at this very moment. Present Continuous ('am doing').

questions.text: She ___ her grandparents next weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Next weekend' is a planned future event. We use Present Continuous ('is visiting').

questions.text: My cat never ___ milk. It only drinks water.
questions.explanation: 'Never' is an adverb of frequency for routines. Cat is 'it', so we use Present Simple with -s ('drinks').

questions.text: Why ___? Is there something funny?
questions.explanation: The person is asking about an action happening at this exact moment. Present Continuous ('are you laughing').

questions.text: We ___ a test this Friday. The teacher told us yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'This Friday' is an organized future event. We use Present Continuous ('are having').

questions.text: The Earth ___ around the Sun.
questions.explanation: This is a universal fact. We always use Present Simple for facts ('goes').

questions.text: Listen! Somebody ___ the piano.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' tells us the action is in progress right now. Present Continuous ('is playing').

questions.text: I ___ to school, but today I am taking the bus because it's raining.
questions.explanation: The first part describes a normal habit ('usually walk' - Present Simple), contrasted with a temporary action today.

questions.text: My friends ___ a party for my birthday tomorrow night.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow night' is a future arrangement. Present Continuous ('are organizing').

questions.text: He ___ English and French fluently.
questions.explanation: Speaking a language is a permanent state/fact, not a temporary action. Present Simple ('speaks').

questions.text: Where is Mum? She ___ dinner in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: The question asks where she is right now, so the action is happening now. Present Continuous ('is making').

questions.text: They ___ to the gym three times a week.
questions.explanation: 'Three times a week' is a routine. We use Present Simple ('go').

questions.text: I ___ my new sneakers tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' indicates a future plan or intention. Present Continuous ('am wearing').

questions.text: Normally it doesn't rain in summer, but it ___ right now.
questions.explanation: 'Right now' indicates the current moment, contrasting with the normal routine. Present Continuous ('is raining').

questions.text: What time ___ up on Sundays?
questions.explanation: 'On Sundays' asks about a routine. We use Present Simple for questions ('do you wake').

questions.text: We ___ for London at 8:00 AM tomorrow. The flight is booked.
questions.explanation: A booked flight is a fixed future arrangement. Present Continuous ('are leaving').
